# Manuscript Figures Gallery (Figs. 1–4) {#figures}

```{r ch9-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
fd <- get_final_data(); eco <- get_eco()
```

All manuscript figures are built directly from the harmonized dataset in `R/figures.R` and `R/ternary.R` and saved to `figs/` as 300 dpi PNG and vector PDF files.

---

## Figure 1: Continental Data Distributions and Ecoregion Coverage {#fig1}

```{r fig1, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 9.5}
p1 <- fig1(fd, eco)
save_fig(p1, 'fig1_distributions_map', 11, 9.5)
p1
```

* **(a)** Probability density distributions of `Chl a` ($\mu\text{g L}^{-1}$), `DOC` ($\text{mg L}^{-1}$), `Secchi` ($\text{m}$), and `TSS` ($\text{mg L}^{-1}$) by water-body type (`Estuary`, `Lake`, `Stream`) across all **`r fmt_n(nrow(fd))`** application matchups, comparing samples with measured Secchi depth (`Measured`, solid lines; $n = `r fmt_n(sum(fd$secchi_status == 'Measured'))`$) against samples where Secchi depth is modeled (`Modeled`, dashed lines; $n = `r fmt_n(sum(fd$secchi_status == 'Modeled'))`$).
* **(b)** Spatial density of matchups aggregated to $0.1^\circ \times 0.1^\circ$ cells over U.S. EPA Level III ecoregions.

---

## Figure 2: Continental Ternary Partitioning by Water-Body Type {#fig2}

```{r fig2, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 8.4}
p2 <- fig2(fd)
save_fig(p2, 'fig2_ternary_by_type', 9, 8.4)
p2
```

Each point represents a sample's non-water light-attenuation fractions $(f_{\text{Chl }a}, f_{\text{DOC}}, f_{\text{NAP}})$ from Model 7 across **(a)** all waters ($n = `r fmt_n(nrow(fd))`$), **(b)** streams ($n = `r fmt_n(sum(fd$type == 'Stream'))`$), **(c)** lakes ($n = `r fmt_n(sum(fd$type == 'Lake'))`$), and **(d)** estuaries ($n = `r fmt_n(sum(fd$type == 'Estuary'))`$). Blue circles mark arithmetic means; red and black polygons enclose $\pm 1\text{ SD}$ and $\pm 2\text{ SD}$ around each mean (`tern_sd_region()`).

---

## Figure 3: Longitudinal River–Estuary Continuum Along the Delaware River and Bay {#fig3}

```{r fig3, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 5.6}
f3 <- get_fig3_data()
p3 <- fig3(f3)
save_fig(p3, 'fig3_delaware', 13, 5.6)
p3
```

Longitudinal shift in light-attenuation partitioning along **231 km** of the Delaware River and Bay across **`r nrow(f3$sites)`** long-term monitoring stations (`31DELRBC_WQX`, $\ge `r P$long_term_min_years`$ distinct years during `r f3$years[1]`–`r f3$years[2]`). Because Model 7 assigns attenuation slopes by Level III ecoregion without imposing a categorical break between `Stream` and `Estuary`, it captures the transition from **DOC dominance** at the head of tide in Trenton (`Site 1, 0 km`) through increasing **NAP dominance** down the tidal river (`Sites 2–4, 41–123 km`) to **DOC–NAP co-dominance and interannual switching** driven by wind and tidal resuspension in Delaware Bay (`Sites 5–6, 180–231 km`).

```{r fig3-table, echo = FALSE}
f3$sites %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% inner_join(DELAWARE_EXEMPLARS, by = 'SiteID') %>%
  left_join(f3$year_avg %>% group_by(SiteID) %>%
              summarize(years = paste(min(year), max(year), sep = '–'),
                        n_years = n(),
                        mean_DOC = percent(mean(doc_kd), 0.1),
                        mean_NAP = percent(mean(tss_kd), 0.1),
                        mean_Chl = percent(mean(chl_kd), 0.1)),
            by = 'SiteID') %>%
  select(num, SiteID, label, type, dist_trenton, years, n_years, mean_DOC, mean_NAP, mean_Chl) %>%
  kable(digits = 0, col.names = c('Panel #', 'WQP SiteID', 'Panel Title', 'WQP Type', 'Distance from Trenton (km)', 'Years Sampled', 'Distinct Years', 'Mean DOC %', 'Mean NAP %', 'Mean Chl a %'),
        caption = 'Long-term Delaware River and Bay monitoring stations highlighted in Panels 1–6 of Figure 3.') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

## Figure 4: Site-Level Temporal Stability — Lucistatic vs. Lucidynamic Regimes {#fig4}

```{r fig4, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 9.5, fig.height = 6.8}
areas <- get_fig4_areas()
p4 <- fig4(fd, areas)
save_fig(p4, 'fig4_area_cdf', 9.5, 6.8)
p4
```

For each station with $> `r P$fig4_min_obs`$ simultaneous matchups (**`r fmt_n(nrow(areas))` sites** across the U.S.), the **ternary area fraction** (`tern_area_fraction()`) measures the share of the equilateral ternary triangle enclosed within $\pm 2\text{ SD}$ of that site's mean composition. Streams (median **`r percent(median(areas$area[areas$type == 'Stream']), 0.1)`**) and estuaries (median **`r percent(median(areas$area[areas$type == 'Estuary']), 0.1)`**) are more temporally compact (*lucistatic*) than lakes (median **`r percent(median(areas$area[areas$type == 'Lake']), 0.1)`**, *lucidynamic*). Fewer than **5%** of lakes (`4.1%`), **3%** of streams (`2.4%`), and **2%** of estuaries (`1.1%`) span $\ge 50\%$ of ternary space.

```{r fig4-medians, echo = FALSE}
areas %>%
  group_by(`Water-Body Type` = type) %>%
  summarize(
    `Sites (> 7 obs)` = fmt_n(n()),
    `25th Percentile` = percent(quantile(area, 0.25), 0.1),
    `Median Area Fraction` = percent(median(area), 0.1),
    `Mean Area Fraction` = percent(mean(area), 0.1),
    `75th Percentile` = percent(quantile(area, 0.75), 0.1),
    `% Sites >= 50% Area` = percent(mean(area >= 0.50), 0.1)
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = 'Distribution of site-level ternary area fractions across water-body types (Figure 4 CDFs).') %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'))
```

```{r fig4-sites, echo = FALSE}
FIG4_SITES %>%
  left_join(areas, by = 'SiteID') %>%
  transmute(
    Inset = inset,
    `CDF Label` = label,
    `WQP SiteID` = SiteID,
    `Station Name` = site_name,
    `Water Type` = type,
    `Observations (n)` = n,
    `Ternary Area Fraction` = percent(area, 0.1),
    `CDF Percentile` = percent(map2_dbl(type, area, ~ ecdf(areas$area[areas$type == .x])(.y)), 0.1),
    `Optical Regime` = role
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = 'The five exemplar monitoring stations highlighted on the CDF curves and Insets 1–3 of Figure 4.') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), font_size = 12, full_width = TRUE)
```
